conditions.displayName: one_scraper_session_blocked >0 in 15m (a real scrape hit a logged-out VM)

documentation.content:
A REAL user scrape found a scraper VM's logged-in browser session unusable, and it needs a HUMAN to clear it (logged out / checkpoint / 2FA / CAPTCHA). This is not a liveness alert — the VM is almost certainly up. Until someone re-logs-in, every scan touching that platform will return shallow or empty results.

Which platform is in the log line (`jsonPayload.platform`).

1. See the failures:
   `gcloud logging read 'jsonPayload.event="one.scraper.session_blocked"' --project hushone-app --freshness=1h --format='value(timestamp,jsonPayload.platform,jsonPayload.accessState)'`
2. Confirm what the VM itself thinks (Instagram example — note the header is `Authorization: Bearer`, NOT `X-API-Key`):
   `curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=instagram-scraper-api-key --project=hushone-app)" http://130.211.224.221:8080/session/status`
   Look at `requiresHumanLogin` / `usableForDeepScrape`.
3. Re-login: open the VM browser over an SSH tunnel and complete the login/2FA by hand, then leave the Chrome window open. See the `scraper-health` skill and `services/instagram-scraper/scripts/gcp-vm/open-login-browser.sh`.

If `accessState` is `rate_limited` or `blocked` this alert will NOT fire (those are WARNING-only and self-clear after the VM's 15-minute cooldown).

Related: the `[one.hushh.ai] dependency DOWN` policy covers DB / Vertex / Deep Research only — scraper VMs are deliberately excluded from it.
